Project

DexArena: A Unified Benchmark for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation

DexArena pairs exact stage slices with their parent long-horizon environments, so isolated skill execution and end-to-end composition can be evaluated without changing the underlying physical setting.

Paper↗Task catalog↗Leaderboard↗Documentation↗
The benchmark at a glance

Dexterous skills, connected into complete behaviors.

Long-horizon manipulation asks a robot to do more than repeat an isolated movement. It must coordinate its fingers and arms, interact precisely with articulated objects, and carry the outcome of one skill into the next. DexArena makes these abilities measurable in a shared physical setting.

The benchmark brings together 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks, spanning six motion categories and household, laboratory and industrial-style scenarios. Each stage is an exact slice of its parent sequence, with matching objects, initialization rules and physical success conditions.

A common interface supports a parallel-jaw gripper, Sharpa Hand, Wuji Hand and XHand. The canonical demonstration release uses Panda arms with Sharpa hands: 3,000 replay-successful episodes, with recorded scene states for restoration and offline rendering.

Six policy baselines are evaluated along three complementary axes: skill execution, visual generalization and long-horizon composition. Separating these questions reveals whether a policy has learned a contact-rich skill, can transfer it to a different scene, and can reliably use it as part of a complete task.

Embodiment

29 dimensions with one hand. 58 with two.

The released canonical data uses Panda arms with 22-DoF Sharpa hands and absolute joint-position targets: 7 arm + 22 hand joints per side.

  • Single-arm and bimanual variants
  • Shared task and success interfaces
  • Parallel-jaw, Sharpa, Wuji, and XHand simulation support

Experimental results

Learning a skill is only the beginning.

Six baselines evaluated on execution, visual generalization and long-horizon composition. All scores below are reported in the supplied manuscript.

Stage execution61.4%

GR00T leads in the training scene.

Average success over 30 stages. ACT reaches 58.0%; RLPD reaches 54.3%.

Visual generalization49.2%

π0.5 leads across held-out scenes.

49.2 ± 2.3% across three kitchens; ACT reaches 45.4 ± 3.6%.

Full task completion1.6%

Composition remains difficult.

π0.5 averages 1.6% across ten complete sequences; ACT reaches 1.2%.
